compute.note: parameters evaluated from the stated architecture: FastLSTMNet, layers = 2, features = [16, 2] (the last layer has hilbert.local_size = 2 features), real float32 parameters. Each LSTM layer l has a kernel (in_l + n_prev f_l) x 4 f_l and a bias 4 f_l, with in_0 = 1 (the spin at the previous site), in_1 = 16, and n_prev = 3 previous neighbours per site: NetKet orders the 100 sites of the graph vmc.py builds (ColoredJ1J2((10, 10), pbc=False, back_diag=False)) greedily and takes the median number of earlier neighbours, rounded up (median 3; evaluated here by re-implementing ordering.py, not by running NetKet). So (1 + 3*16)*64 + 64 = 3200 and (16 + 3*2)*8 + 8 = 184, total 3384. samples = 1024 per optimisation step (MCState n_samples = batch_size; ARDirectSampler (autoregressive, one pass per sample)); iterations = 100000 (--max_step 100000); optimizer Adam, lr 1e-3. The final energy is then estimated once with estim_size = 1024^2 = 1048576 samples (not an optimisation step). NetKet pinned twice by the program: programs/vmc_netket/requirements.txt "NetKet==3.13.0" and conda_env.yaml "netket=3.11.4"; every NetKet line cited here reads the same at both tags. The energy is older than the script: VarBench's data file listed it with no code link ("TODO: own code", varbench/varbench 0ef1497c and 6e9f6b83, 2024-07-11) until the scripts were added on 2024-07-30 (5047bfd6 RBM, d54f7c01 RNN, 765c5d13 GCNN), which changed only the reference column, so the script documents the settings after the fact, with library versions that may postdate the run.

compute.reported_as: During the training, we use Adam optimizer with batch size 1,024 for all reported results, and we have found that the stochastic reconfiguration (SR) and the plain stochastic gradient descent (SGD) generally produce higher variational energies within the same number of training steps or wall-clock time. Gradient clipping with global norm 1 is applied to alleviate the energy spikes. After the training, each reported variational energy is estimated from 10^6 samples, and its statistical error is too small to be visible in the plots. [...] For bond dimensions chi <= 10, we use learning rate 1e-2 for 10,000 steps, 1e-3 for another 10,000 steps, and finally 1e-4 for 20,000 steps. We manually reduce the learning rate by a factor of 10 if we find the variational energy diverges in the middle of training. For bond dimensions chi > 10, we start from learning rate 1e-3. The training of a tensor-RNN with chi = 64 on the 10 x 10 triangular AFHM takes about 2 days on an Nvidia V100 GPU. || method string: "1D MPS-RNN (bond dimension = 40)"
compute.source: Supplemental Material Sec. S7 'Details of numerical experiments' (arXiv:2206.12363v2 = Phys. Rev. Research 5, L032001; published PDF checked, identical text), arXiv:2206.12363 (compute pass 2026-09-16)
compute.note: Blanket statement for all reported results. samples = 1024 is the Adam batch size per training step; the final energies are evaluated from 1e6 samples. The only device/wall-clock statement ('about 2 days on an Nvidia V100 GPU') is for the tensor-RNN with chi = 64 on the 10x10 triangular lattice, which is not the bond dimension of this row, so device/wall_clock are left null here. Step count is stated only for chi <= 10 (40,000 steps total); for chi > 10 only the starting learning rate is given. Parameter counts are shown only graphically (Fig. S3, energy error vs number of parameters), no number stated; static memory scales as O(V chi^2) for 1D/2D MPS-RNN and O(V chi^3) for tensor-RNN. bond_dimension is left null because the worklist's chi (40 for 10x10, 64 for the 20x20 TFIM) is not stated as a number in the paper text (Fig. 4 plots energy vs chi without a table; the 20x20 TFIM appears only in Fig. S4(b) with chi = 16). Worklist had no arXiv id; arXiv 2206.12363 read from the repo cache.

compute.note: Parameters evaluated: NetKet 3.13.0 Jastrow stores the strictly lower triangle of W, N(N-1)/2 = 100*99/2 = 4950 real (float32) weights, which is also what vmc.py prints as n_params (tree_size_real_nonzero). Samples: 1024 per SR step, 1024 chains of length 1, each sample one sweep of 100 exchange proposals, no discard. Iterations: 10^4 steps (--max_step default). Driver: nkx.driver.VMC_SRt (n_parameters >= n_samples = 1024). After training the energy is estimated from 2^20 samples. stored sigma 0.0093 vs sqrt(stored variance 87.62059 / 2^20) = 0.0091: consistent with the script's 2^20-sample final estimate (--estim_size default). Provenance: the value entered VarBench in 59e621a (2022-09-13, Dian Wu); the linked script was added to varbench/methods in c686621 (2024-07-30) without the value changing, so the script is the authors' later reconstruction of the baseline, not a log of the run (the same holds for the TFIsing RBM rows, scripts/defects.mjs). The 2^20-sample final estimate is corroborated by the stored sigma; batch size and step count are not independently corroborated. No device or time is recorded (the conda env includes CUDA; the README says a GPU is "usually needed for VMC on larger lattices", which is not a statement about these runs).
